text:
Faculty Review
Faculty Initial: SOJ
Course: PHI401
The course content is quite easy and very manageable. Sir makes the course simple for students and is always willing to answer questions if you ask him. However, his teaching style can feel a bit monotonous at times since he mostly teaches by reading from the slides or a script. Despite that, he explains the concepts clearly enough for students to perform well in the course.
Course Breakdown:
* 3 Quizzes (Counts 2)
* 1 Midterm (30%)
* Attendance and participation (10%)
* Final Exam (40%)
There are no reports or presentations in this course.
The quizzes are easy to score. Each quiz consists of 6 MCQs and 2 short questions, and most of the questions come directly from the lecture materials. If you go through the slides properly, you shouldn’t have much difficulty.
The midterm and final are also straightforward. One of the best things is that Sir always provides a sample question before the exams. The sample question closely reflect the actual exam, and you’ll usually find questions that appear in a very similar form in both the midterm and final. He usually gives the same sample question in the exam. This gives you a good idea of what to expect.
The final exam mainly requires descriptive answers, where you often have to explain topics in detail. Although the questions can seem lengthy, the syllabus is quite manageable. We only had to study two chapters for the final, making preparation much easier.
Sir is also a lenient marker, so scoring good marks is definitely possible if you study the course materials. One thing to be careful about is attendance. He calculates attendance marks very strictly, so even missing a single class can reduce your attendance score.
One thing worth mentioning is that our class was extremely competitive. A large number of students performed exceptionally well, and almost half of the class scored 90% or above overall. Because of this, Sir had to count grades very precisely, even considering differences as small as 0.40 marks when assigning the final letter grades. So while scoring high is definitely possible, even a tiny difference in marks can affect your final grade in such a competitive class.
Overall, this is one of the easier electives to take. The teaching style may not be the most engaging, but the course is student-friendly, the exams are predictable, and it’s a good option if you’re looking for a faculty who is easy-going for this course.

So yes, if you have practiced well the slides, the class maths, and the marked maths, you are good to go for the mids and finals. Her questions are a bit lengthy so you would need to practice a lot so that you can finish in time.
For the assignment: It's a bit easy. You can do it and you can seek help from her too.

ENG103 (NNM) - I had a hard time following her lectures because they were boring and she was also very uncooperative, but could be because of the online classes. Her quizzes and exams were easy but I felt she did not grade students fairly, and was biased.
POL101 (RZK) - For me, the course itself was not very interesting so I felt sir’s teaching was average as well. I did not enjoy it, but I could get through it. Sir made questions directly from the slides and also grades fairly. 
ECO101 (MUF) - Sir is very old, so I was very grateful that he made so much efforts to teach us, that to online. The lectures weren’t fun tho, exams were not easy neither hard, and he graded fairly. 
MGT212 and MKT330 (ZMC) - In both the courses I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She puts a lot of efforts into making the lectures enjoyable and she also gives hints about the exams. She grades very strictly but fairly. But most importantly she’s very compassionate and empathetic towards her students and excuses a lot of things simply for them to pass the course. 
MKT202 and MKT344 (FCH) - Her lectures are very elaborative and she makes sure all the students understand them. She gives a lot of opportunities for bonus marking as well. She is very strict tho but as long as you are a attentive and sincere student you’re good to go. Are exams are tricky and critical and she grades fairly. She’s also very no-nonsense.
ACT201 (FJM) - His teaching style is average, but his grading is biased. He’s also a little rude. I would not suggest to take his course. 
ECO104 (NNM) - Miss is very sweet, she teaches really well. Her exams aren’t very hard either and her grading style is fair. 
LAW200 (TTR) - Again, miss is really sweet. I really enjoyed her exams. She’s also very understanding. Her exams are easy to score in, and she grades fairly. 
ENG105 (RT1) - Just drop the courses. She’s inconsiderate, uncooperative and does not teach well. I dropped it before my mids. 
ACT202 (RMH1) - I think sir is one of the best faculties for this course. He teaches really well, his exams are easy to perform in if you follow his lecture and he grades fairly. 
BUS172 (KHS) - Sir is very strict but he’s also probably one of the best faculties in NSU. He teaches extremely well, is also very helpful. And he curves a lot. 
ENG105 (MCD) - She’s very strict, but she teaches really well. She’ll do her best to guide you in every step so that you get the grade you deserve. 
INB372 (TFZ) - Miss is fun and caring. Her teaching style is easy to catch. Her exams are super easy too and she grades really well. 
PHI401 (BAI) - I had a hard time with this course, but I think PHI is just boring and not really Sir’s fault. He gives a lot of chances to makeup for any lost grade. 
BUS251 (UHM) - One of my favourite faculties. The course itself is very easy and UMH makes it a walk in the park. Her activities are really fun and she gives a lot of chances to score. She also prepares you really well for the exams so there’s no chance that you won’t get your deserving grade. 
PSY101 (FHK) - Miss is really fun. Even though it’s offline classes now she takes the quizzes online. She is very generous with marking too. 
SOC101 (IZS) - I saved it for the last because miss has some very controversial reviews. Yes it is a GED course and yet miss makes you work very hard for it. You have to watch movies, tons of videos, read the slides, books, and other materials to score well. But she also teaches really well, her classes are fun to follow and very interactive. She also grades very well. You just need to study. 
BUS173 (RSJ) - Ma’am taught amazingly. I struggle with maths but she made it reality easy to catch on. She also gave students chances to sit for exams if they missed it due to proper reason. Her exams were also not hard. However, I felt like she was biased and helped her favourite students during exams and hence she might not have graded us all fairly.

HRM340 (FSZ):
Quizzes are conceptual, and the important slides will be marked. For the written part, she’ll give suggestions-questions will come from there. Her exams aren’t that tough; just go through the important slides and her suggestions.

For the poster, put in all your creativity and effort because that will matter the most.
PSY101 (Nak1):
Attend all the classes, be attentive, and take notes on everything she says because everything will come from there. If you don’t take notes, you won’t be able to do well, as reading the slides won’t help at all. The slides are very brief and mostly contain terms without in-depth explanations or descriptions.
Quiz 1 and 2 are going to be easy - do well in those so you can skip Quiz 3. For the midterm, she will give 5 MCQs worth 2 marks each, so be careful with those and don’t overwrite. The written part is very conceptual - attending the classes will be enough to handle them.
There will be one reflective assignment. Just follow her instructions and you’ll be good to go. Don’t expect any curving; you’ll get exactly what you earn.
Other than that, she’s very sweet and friendly. She keeps the class interactive and doesn’t stretch it unnecessarily - she usually ends the class within an hour or so. Also, try to participate in class as much as possible - she really appreciates that.

Faculty review for PHI401[RDN] Ms. Ridma Khan ma'am.
1. Ma'am has a great personality. With my NSU life near to an end, I have rarely seen such a caring and affectionate teacher like RDN miss. She teaches very well and is a great mentor and guide. She is very linient, gives good grades and curves a little based on overall class performance. 
2. Classes are very interesting and imformative. Ma'am uses real-life examples & scenarios to explain each topic. You will get to learn a lot from her. She is a wonderful human being.
3. She speakes a little fast, so lectures end quickly. But if the students want she goes slowly. And always elaborates/deeply explains if anyone has any confusion. She even goes through a single topic multiple times if students don't understand.
4. Class participation and response is very important. Ma'am evaluates each students based on their class participation, depth of knowledge & interest over the subject.
5. For Phi401 there will be a very easy group assignment of 2-3 pages and a final group report plus presentation over the "Ethical Issues in a Corporation". Students can form their own groups and select companies. Ma'am will help you through these works. Participation of all members is very important.
6. There are 3 quizes, 2mids and a final. Quiz will be on 1/2 chapters, Mids on 2 chapters and final on 2/3 chapters. Quizes will be mostly T/F, MCQ, and 2line questions total 10marks.
7. Mid1 is a little conceptual with S/Q, B/Q. Mid2 and Final are more direct with MCQ, S/Q & B/Q. Mid 1 & 2 is of 15marks and 30min will be given.
Final is of 25marks and 60min will be given.
8. Take class notes and also note down the important examples and topics ma'am tells in class. Also note down the things she writes on board. These things definitely comes in the exams. All questions will be from the slides, pages she mentions from the book and the oral lectures she gives.
9. To get an A/A- be attentive, regular and participative in class from the very first day. Always ask questions if there is any confusion. She is very helpful. Contact her via email if you have any course related issues.

Faculty Reviews - Spring 2026
FIN444 - TNK (Dr. Tanvir Nabi Khan)

The course itself is very easy. Tanvir sir is super chill too (and has a very niche sense of humor 
). He shows all of the maths in Excel, so if you want to understand what is being taught, you need to be a bit more attentive than usual. Otherwise, you can self-study, as the maths are pretty easy. The theories are very straightforward too. He takes three quizzes and counts the best two. The quizzes have MCQs and/or maths. There are two mids, which include short questions and maths. The final consists of MCQs, short questions, and maths. I personally found his questions to be very easy; only the MCQs of the final were just a tad bit tricky. There is a very basic group assignment. His marking is very, very lenient, and I think he curves based on class performance.
MGT368 - SAI2 (Mr. Shabab Absarul Islam)

Shabab sir is hands down the most easygoing faculty for this course. His lectures are short and fun to attend. He highlights all of the important questions from the slides. He takes two to three quizzes and drops the worst one. There are two case studies. There is an individual entrepreneurial case assignment and a group project, along with a presentation. He’s quite lenient in grading these assessments. That said, the project is huge, and you’ll definitely need a good group. There are MCQs, T/F, short, and broad questions in the mid and final, and the questions are based on his suggestions. He curves according to the section’s overall performance as well.
ACT202 - FI (Dr. Farhana Islam)

Farhana ma’am is extremely easygoing. It’s a bit difficult to stay attentive in her class, but the course is very basic, so self-studying is the key. She highlights important theories and maths from the book, and you will find EXACTLY the same questions in the exams, just with different values (and sometimes even with the same values). There is a very simple group project. Her marking is lenient, and she curves too.
PHI401 - ZkH1 (Dr. Zakir Hossain)

Zakir sir is a gentleman, but his lectures aren’t that engaging. He takes three quizzes and counts the best two. Quizzes include MCQs and case-based questions. The mid and the final consist of short and broad questions. The questions are based on his class lectures and slides, but the MCQs in the quizzes are a bit tough. His marking in the subjective portion is a bit vague as well. There is a fairly basic group report and presentation, followed by an individual viva, and he grades all of these generously. Overall, he’s nice, but I’m not sure whether he curves or not. Still, it’s definitely possible to get a good grade from him.
ENV107 - ARK (Dr. Md. Anisur Rahman Khan)

Anisur sir is a jolly-minded person, but his lectures are super-duper boring, and so is the course itself. He takes three quizzes and counts the best two. The quizzes include MCQs, fill-in-the-blank questions, and short questions. There are two mids and a final, where the question pattern is similar to the quizzes. He gives general suggestions long before the exams (which basically cover almost everything from the slides xD). However, right before the exams, he provides very short suggestions, which are helpful. But there’s a catch: he teaches a lot of chapters, and the slides are also massive. So, if you aren’t good at rote memorization, it’s gonna be difficult to score good marks in his course. He takes an individual assignment and an individual presentation, which he grades liberally. Overall, his marking is lenient, and he curves too.
